blogs.title: When 'Angioedema' Isn't Angioedema: The Great Mimics of Neck Swelling
blogs.description: A deep dive into the diagnostic challenge of acute neck swelling. This post analyzes the clinical trajectory from suspected Ludwig's angina to idiopathic angioedema, eventually uncovering a rare presentation of dermatomyositis. We discuss how to differentiate histamine- and bradykinin-mediated edema from inflammatory pseudo-angioedema and provide a broadened differential for the ED physician when the 'obvious' causes of swelling are ruled out.

blogs.title: More Than a Rash: Recognizing Atypical Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Dermatomyositis is often taught as a 'textbook' rash (Heliotrope and Gottron's papules). However, this case demonstrates a presentation where cutaneous signs were subtle. This post focuses on the 'hidden' clues clinicians should look for, including nailfold capillaroscopy changes, the 'holster sign,' and the critical importance of ordering a creatine kinase (CK) level in patients with unexplained systemic inflammation and muscle weakness.

blogs.title: The Silent Airway Threat: Dysphagia and Aspiration in Myositis
blogs.description: Inflammatory myopathies aren't just about proximal limb weakness; they can be life-threatening when they hit the pharyngeal muscles. This post discusses the risk of 'silent' aspiration and aspiration pneumonitis in dermatomyositis, the utility of video fluoroscopic swallow studies in these patients, and why early recognition of dysphagia is critical to prevent respiratory failure.

blogs.title: The Paraneoplastic Puzzle: Cancer Screening in Inflammatory Myopathies
blogs.description: Dermatomyositis can be the first herald of an occult malignancy. Using the IMACS guidelines as a framework, this post explores how to risk-stratify patients for cancer based on age, sex, and specific autoantibodies (like anti-SAE1). We discuss the tension between aggressive screening (PET scans, endoscopies) and the clinical evidence of malignancy in myositis patients.
